name: Name the Countries
tagline: Type every country you can remember before time runs out
description: Type as many countries as you can from memory before time runs out — no options, no hints, just what you actually know. Play all 195 at once, or pick a single starting letter.
metaTitle: Name the Countries — Free-Recall Geography Quiz
metaDescription: Type as many countries as you can from memory before time runs out. Play all 195 countries, or pick a single starting letter, from A to Z.
guide: Every other game here shows you four options and asks you to recognise the right one. This is the opposite: a blank box and a clock, and nothing comes up unless you can actually produce it from memory. That is a much harder and much more honest test of what you know.

Common short names and spelling variants are accepted — type USA, America or United States and all three count, and the same goes for Ivory Coast, Czechia, Myanmar and a handful of other countries with more than one widely used name. There is no partial credit for a near-miss spelling of a name the list does not recognise, so precision still matters.

Most people stall somewhere between twenty and forty countries, usually after clearing the obvious ones — the large countries, the countries in the news, the ones they have visited. The next fifty come from Africa, the Pacific and Central Asia, and that is exactly the geography the rest of the site's games are built to fill in.

name: Border Quiz
tagline: Name a country that shares a border
description: Given a country, pick one of its land neighbours. Knowing who borders whom is the part of a map that names and flags never teach you.
metaTitle: Border Quiz — Which Countries Share a Border?
metaDescription: Play a free border quiz. Given a country, identify one of its land neighbours across four difficulty levels.
guide: Borders are the relationships a map is actually made of. You can know every flag and capital and still have no idea that Turkey borders Georgia, or that China has fourteen land neighbours — more than any country except Russia, which has the same number.

The wrong answers are always drawn from the same continent and are never neighbours, so there is exactly one correct choice and no way to get there by elimination. On the harder levels that means four plausible countries from the same region, only one of which actually touches the target.

Thirty-nine countries never appear as the subject here because they have no land borders at all — island states like Japan, Iceland, Cuba and the Philippines, plus Australia. Their absence is itself worth noticing.

name: Country Quiz
tagline: Identify the country from a set of clues
description: Read the capital, continent and currency, then name the country. A great way to connect facts that are usually learned separately.
metaTitle: Country Quiz — Guess the Country from Clues
metaDescription: Play a free country quiz. Identify countries from their capital city, continent and currency across four difficulty levels.
guide: The country quiz is the hardest of the name-based games because it gives you no picture to lean on. You get a capital, a continent and a currency, and have to work backwards to the country. That is a genuinely different skill from recognising a flag: it tests whether the facts are connected in your memory or merely stored side by side.

The currency line is usually the most useful clue. West African CFA franc narrows the field to eight countries in one stroke; Central African CFA franc to six others. Learning which countries share a currency does more work here than memorising any individual capital.
If a round feels impossible, the gap is usually capitals rather than countries. Play the capital quiz on the same difficulty for a few rounds and come back.

name: Map Quiz
tagline: Find the country on the world map
description: You get a country name and a map. Click the right country. The map zooms to the surrounding region so even smaller countries stay easy to hit on a phone.
metaTitle: World Map Quiz — Find the Country on the Map
metaDescription: Play a free world map quiz. Click countries on an interactive map across four difficulty levels and learn where every country is.
guide: Knowing a country's name and knowing where it is are separate skills, and most quizzes only test the first. This one puts a map in front of you and asks you to point.

The map zooms to the region around the target so smaller countries stay large enough to tap on a phone. That means you are given the neighbourhood and asked to find the country inside it, which is closer to how you would actually read an atlas.

Not every country appears. At world scale the smallest states are a few pixels across, so the map quiz draws on the 154 countries that are large enough to identify and tap reliably. The shape quiz covers 163 on a similar basis.

name: Country Shape Quiz
tagline: Name the country from its outline
description: One silhouette, four names. No flags, no capitals, no borders drawn in — just the shape of the country, which is how most people actually picture a map.
metaTitle: Country Shape Quiz — Guess the Country by Its Outline
metaDescription: Play a free country shape quiz. Identify countries from their outline alone, from easy silhouettes to expert ones.
guide: Ask someone to picture Italy and they will see the boot, not the flag or the capital. Outlines are how most people actually store a map, and this is the only game here that tests that directly.

Some silhouettes are unmistakable: Italy, Chile, Norway, India, Japan. Others are far harder than you would expect, because a country's shape is the part of it we rehearse least. Landlocked states in central Africa and central Asia give almost nothing away.
Outlines are drawn at world-map scale and then enlarged, so tiny states are excluded — 163 of the 195 countries have an outline distinct enough to be worth asking about.

name: Landlocked Countries
tagline: Click every landlocked country, continent by continent
description: Every country in a continent, in one list. Click only the landlocked ones — sudden death, one wrong click ends the run.
metaTitle: Landlocked Countries Quiz — Europe, Africa & Asia
metaDescription: Test what you know about the world's landlocked countries. Pick Europe, Africa or Asia, then click every landlocked one before a wrong click ends the run.
guide: Forty-four of the world's countries have no coastline, and all but two of them are in Europe, Africa or Asia. Each continent below is its own quiz, because the countries involved — and how well most people know them — are different enough that lumping them together would just mean more coastal-Europe questions and fewer real ones about Central Asia.
The exceptions are South America, which has only two landlocked countries, and North America and Oceania, which have none at all — worth knowing, but not enough material for a quiz of their own.

Every country in the continent is on screen at once. Click the ones you think are landlocked; a correct click marks it and keeps you going, a wrong click ends the round immediately. Your score is how many you found before the mistake — or all of them, if you clear the whole list.

name: Landlocked Countries: Europe
tagline: Click every landlocked country — one wrong click ends it
description: Every country in Europe, in one list. Click only the landlocked ones — sudden death, one wrong click ends the run.
metaTitle: Landlocked Countries in Europe Quiz — Sudden Death
metaDescription: Can you click all 14 of Europe's landlocked countries without a single mistake? Free sudden-death geography quiz — one wrong click ends the run.
guide: Fourteen of Europe's countries have no coastline — more than any other continent — and they cluster in two bands: the Alps (Switzerland, Austria, Liechtenstein), the old Soviet and Yugoslav interior (Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia, Belarus, Moldova, Serbia, North Macedonia), plus three of the world's smallest states, Luxembourg, Andorra, San Marino and Vatican City.

Liechtenstein is one of only two countries on Earth that are doubly landlocked — surrounded entirely by other landlocked countries, Switzerland and Austria — so reaching the sea from Vaduz means crossing at least two borders.

Being landlocked here is no handicap: Switzerland, Austria and Luxembourg are among the wealthiest countries in the world, proof that the real cost is about market access rather than coastline as such.

name: Landlocked Countries: Africa
tagline: Click every landlocked country — one wrong click ends it
description: Every country in Africa, in one list. Click only the landlocked ones — sudden death, one wrong click ends the run.
metaTitle: Landlocked Countries in Africa Quiz — Sudden Death
metaDescription: Can you click all 16 of Africa's landlocked countries without a single mistake? Free sudden-death geography quiz — one wrong click ends the run.
guide: Africa has sixteen landlocked countries, the largest concentration on Earth, running from the Sahel — Mali, Niger, Chad, Burkina Faso, the Central African Republic — down through South Sudan and Ethiopia to a cluster in Central and Southern Africa: Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Botswana, Lesotho and Eswatini.

Ethiopia is the largest population anywhere in the world without a coastline. It lost its own coast when Eritrea became independent in 1993, and its trade has depended on the port of Djibouti ever since.
Lesotho is entirely enclosed by South Africa — one of only three such enclaves in the world, alongside Vatican City and San Marino inside Italy.

name: Landlocked Countries: Asia
tagline: Click every landlocked country — one wrong click ends it
description: Every country in Asia, in one list. Click only the landlocked ones — sudden death, one wrong click ends the run.
metaTitle: Landlocked Countries in Asia Quiz — Sudden Death
metaDescription: Can you click all 12 of Asia's landlocked countries without a single mistake? Free sudden-death geography quiz — one wrong click ends the run.
guide: Asia's twelve landlocked countries are mostly former Soviet Central Asia and its neighbours: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, plus Afghanistan, Mongolia, Nepal, Bhutan, Laos, Armenia and Azerbaijan.
Uzbekistan is the world's other doubly landlocked country — every one of its five neighbours is itself landlocked, so its goods cross at least two borders before reaching open water.

Whether Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan actually give Uzbekistan a way out depends on whether the Caspian Sea counts as a sea at all — a genuine, decades-old legal argument, since under the usual reading it is an enclosed lake with no outlet to the ocean.

name: Reverse Capital Quiz
tagline: Name the country from its capital city
description: The capital quiz backwards. You get a city — Bishkek, Asunción, Lusaka — and have to name the country it governs.
metaTitle: Reverse Capital Quiz — Name the Country from Its Capital
metaDescription: Play a free reverse capital quiz. Given a capital city, name the country it belongs to, from easy to expert.
guide: Recall in one direction does not give you the other. Plenty of people can answer "what is the capital of Mongolia" and stall completely on "Ulaanbaatar is the capital of where" — the link was learned one way round and only works that way.

This game is the fastest way to find those one-directional gaps. If you score noticeably worse here than on the ordinary capital quiz, your capitals are memorised as answers to a specific question rather than as facts you actually hold.
No continent hint is shown with the city, deliberately. Naming the region would eliminate most of the wrong answers before you had thought about the question at all.

name: Capital Quiz
tagline: Guess the capital city of a country
description: One country, four cities, thirty questions. Capitals are the fastest route to knowing a map, and the wrong answers come from the same region to keep it honest.
metaTitle: Capital Cities Quiz — Guess the Capital of Every Country
metaDescription: Play a free world capitals quiz. Guess the capital city of countries from every continent, from easy to expert difficulty.
guide: Capitals are the hardest basic geography facts to hold because nothing about the name points to the country. There is no visual hook the way there is with a flag, and no logic connecting Bishkek to Kyrgyzstan. Repetition with immediate correction is the only thing that reliably works, which is what this game is built around.

The wrong answers are drawn from the same continent as the correct one, so elimination by region will not save you. On expert rounds you will regularly see four plausible Central Asian or West African capitals together.

A handful catch almost everyone out: Bolivia's constitutional capital is Sucre rather than La Paz, South Africa's seat of government is Pretoria, Sri Lanka's is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte rather than Colombo, and Myanmar moved its capital to Naypyidaw in 2005.

name: Flag Quiz
tagline: Identify countries from their flags
description: See a flag, name the country. Distractors are drawn from the same continent, so the expert rounds are genuinely difficult.
metaTitle: Flag Quiz — Guess the Country by Its Flag
metaDescription: Play a free world flags quiz. Identify all 195 country flags across easy, medium, hard and expert difficulty.
guide: Flags are the fastest route into world geography because they are visual. Most people can recognise a flag long before they can recall the matching capital, and that recognition then acts as a hook for everything else about the country.

The hard rounds lean on genuine near-duplicates. Chad and Romania are almost indistinguishable. Monaco and Indonesia differ only in proportion. Ireland and Ivory Coast are mirror images. Australia and New Zealand both carry the Union Jack and the Southern Cross, differing in the number and colour of the stars.
Flags render using your device's own emoji font, so the exact drawing style depends on your operating system. The colours and layout are the same everywhere.

name: Find the Flag
tagline: Pick the right flag for a named country
description: The flag quiz in reverse: you get the country and choose its flag from four. Recognising a flag is easy; producing it from memory is not.
metaTitle: Find the Flag — Pick the Correct Flag for Each Country
metaDescription: Play a free find-the-flag quiz. Given a country name, choose its flag from four options across four difficulty levels.
guide: Recognition and recall are different skills, and flags flatter the first. Shown Ghana's flag you may well name it; asked to picture Ghana's flag from the name alone, most people find they cannot. This game tests the harder direction.

Because the wrong flags come from the same continent, the design families do most of the work against you. Four West African flags in red, gold and green look far more alike than any two flags picked at random.
Flags are drawn with your device's own emoji font, so the exact style depends on your operating system. Colours and layout are identical everywhere.

name: Continent Quiz
tagline: Place every country on the right continent
description: The quickest game on the site and the best starting point. Given a country, choose the continent it belongs to.
metaTitle: Continent Quiz — Which Continent Is Each Country In?
metaDescription: Play a free continents quiz. Match all 195 countries to Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America or Oceania.
guide: This is the fastest game on the site and the best place to start if geography is new to you. Six possible answers, no memorisation of names required, and it builds the mental map that every other game hangs off.

The awkward cases are the ones that straddle a boundary. Russia and Turkey span Europe and Asia; this site places Russia in Europe and Turkey in Asia, following the most common convention. Cyprus, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan are counted as Asia. Central America and the Caribbean sit under North America, which surprises a lot of players.
Egypt has territory on both sides of the Suez Canal and is counted as Africa throughout.

name: Currency Quiz
tagline: Match countries to the money they use
description: Which currency does Vietnam use? Currencies group countries in ways borders do not, and learning them makes the country quiz considerably easier.
metaTitle: Currency Quiz — Which Currency Does Each Country Use?
metaDescription: Play a free world currency quiz. Match countries to their currencies, from the euro and the CFA franc to the ngultrum.
guide: Currencies are the most useful clue in the whole of geography and the least studied. The West African CFA franc narrows a question to eight countries in one stroke; the Central African CFA franc to six others; the euro to twenty.

Shared currencies also tell you real history. The two CFA francs trace French colonial administration, the East Caribbean dollar ties together seven small island states, and Ecuador, El Salvador, Timor-Leste and several Pacific nations use the US dollar outright rather than issuing their own.
This is the game that most improves your score elsewhere. The country quiz gives you a currency as one of its three clues, and knowing the currency groups turns that from decoration into an answer.

name: Language Quiz
tagline: Name the main language of each country
description: The main language of a country traces its history more directly than almost anything else on a map — trade, empire, migration and independence all leave their mark.
metaTitle: Language Quiz — What Language Does Each Country Speak?
metaDescription: Play a free world language quiz. Match countries to their main language across every continent and four difficulty levels.
guide: Language maps and political maps rarely agree, which is what makes this interesting. Portuguese is the main language of Angola and Mozambique but of no country between them; Spanish is official in Equatorial Guinea and nowhere else in Africa; French reaches from Belgium to Vanuatu.

The surprises are worth collecting. Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas. Suriname is the only Dutch-speaking one. Malagasy, spoken in Madagascar off the African coast, is most closely related to a language of Borneo, some 7,000 kilometres away.

This site lists one main language per country for the sake of a clean question. Many countries have several official languages — South Africa recognises twelve, India twenty-two at national level — so treat the answer as the principal one rather than the only one.

name: Mixed Geography Quiz
tagline: Random questions from every category
description: Flags, capitals, continents, landmarks and oceans shuffled into one round. The closest thing on the site to a general geography test.
metaTitle: Mixed Geography Quiz — Flags, Capitals, Countries and More
metaDescription: Play a free mixed geography quiz combining flags, capitals, countries, continents, landmarks and oceans in one round.
guide: The mixed quiz pulls from flags, capitals, countries, continents, landmarks and oceans in a single round. It is the closest thing here to an honest general test, and it is the fastest way to find out which category is letting you down.

Because questions rotate between categories, you cannot settle into one kind of thinking. That makes it noticeably harder than any single game at the same difficulty, even though the individual questions are drawn from the same pools.
This is also the game behind the daily challenge, where every player gets the same thirty questions, generated from the date so they change at midnight.

name: Oceans & Seas Quiz
tagline: Learn the oceans and the major seas
description: Five oceans and twenty-five major seas, described one at a time. The part of the map most quizzes ignore.
metaTitle: Oceans and Seas Quiz — Name the World's Waters
metaDescription: Play a free oceans and seas quiz. Identify the five oceans and the major seas of the world from short descriptions.
guide: Oceans and seas are the part of the map most quizzes skip entirely, which is odd given that water covers most of the planet. This game covers the five oceans and twenty-five of the major seas.

Each question describes a body of water and asks you to name it. That framing rewards understanding over rote recall — knowing that a sea is almost enclosed, or that it connects two others through a narrow strait, is more useful than memorising a list.

A few are worth knowing before you start: the Caspian is the largest inland body of water on Earth and has no outlet to the ocean, and the Southern Ocean was only formally recognised as distinct in 2000.

name: Top Spoken Languages
tagline: Name a continent's most-spoken languages from memory
description: Type as many of a continent's top languages by native speakers as you can before time runs out. Pick a continent to start.
metaTitle: Top Spoken Languages Quiz — By Continent
metaDescription: Can you name the most-spoken languages on each continent? Free typing quiz, ranked by native speakers, for Europe, Asia, Africa and more.
guide: Each continent's list is ranked by native speakers, not by where a language is officially recognised or how many people speak it as a second language — that single rule is what makes six very different lists comparable to each other.

That convention produces some genuinely surprising results. Swahili is understood by well over a hundred million people across East Africa but ranks low here, because almost all of them learned it as a second language rather than a first.

Some continents give a full top ten; North America and Oceania stop at six, because beyond that point sources disagree even on which languages belong on the list, not just their order — a shorter, honest list beats a longer, made-up one.

name: Top Spoken Languages: Europe
tagline: Name Europe's most-spoken languages from memory
description: Europe's top 10 languages by native speakers. Type as many as you can before time runs out.
metaTitle: Top 10 Spoken Languages in Europe Quiz
metaDescription: Can you name the 10 most-spoken languages in Europe by native speakers? Free typing quiz — race the clock before time runs out.
guide: Russian tops this list, which surprises people who forget how much of Russia's population is west of the Urals and therefore counted as Europe on most maps, including this site's. German, French and English follow closely, all in the 65–85 million range.
Spanish and Italian both sit in the 40–60 million band — Spanish counted here only for Spain itself, since the huge Spanish-speaking population of the Americas is on a different continent.
Polish, Ukrainian, Romanian and Dutch round out the list. Notably absent: Turkish, spoken by tens of millions, but overwhelmingly in Turkey — which this site, like most conventions, counts as Asia.

name: Top Spoken Languages: Asia
tagline: Name Asia's most-spoken languages from memory
description: Asia's top 10 languages by native speakers. Type as many as you can before time runs out.
metaTitle: Top 10 Spoken Languages in Asia Quiz
metaDescription: Can you name the 10 most-spoken languages in Asia by native speakers? Free typing quiz — race the clock before time runs out.
guide: Mandarin Chinese leads by a wide margin, with close to a billion native speakers — more than the next three languages on this list combined.

Hindi and Bengali follow, both concentrated in South Asia, ahead of Arabic, Punjabi and Japanese. Cantonese, Turkish and Marathi round out the bottom of the ten, all within a few million of each other.

The bottom of this list is genuinely close: Telugu, Korean, Tamil and Urdu are all within a few million speakers of the countries that made the cut, so a slightly different source could reorder the last two or three places.

name: Top Spoken Languages: Africa
tagline: Name Africa's most-spoken languages from memory
description: Africa's top 10 languages by native speakers. Type as many as you can before time runs out.
metaTitle: Top 10 Spoken Languages in Africa Quiz
metaDescription: Can you name the 10 most-spoken languages in Africa by native speakers? Free typing quiz — race the clock before time runs out.
guide: Arabic leads Africa's list too, spread across Egypt, Sudan and the whole of North Africa. Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo follow — all three concentrated in and around Nigeria, the continent's most populous country by a wide margin.

Swahili is the list's odd entry: as a native language it ranks near the bottom here, but as a second language it is understood by well over a hundred million people across East and Central Africa, arguably the continent's most useful lingua franca.
Portuguese closes out the list on the strength of Angola alone, where it has become a first language for a fast-growing share of the urban population.

name: Top Spoken Languages: South America
tagline: Name South America's most-spoken languages from memory
description: South America's top 10 languages by native speakers. Type as many as you can before time runs out.
metaTitle: Top 10 Spoken Languages in South America Quiz
metaDescription: Can you name the 10 most-spoken languages in South America by native speakers? Free typing quiz — race the clock before time runs out.
guide: Portuguese and Spanish are almost tied at the top, both around 215 million — Portuguese carried entirely by Brazil, Spanish spread across the other twelve countries.
Everything after that is a steep drop: Quechua, the largest Indigenous language, has around 8 million speakers, less than 4% of Portuguese's total.

Guarani is the rare Indigenous language with genuine official status alongside Spanish, in Paraguay, where most of the population speaks it. German, Italian and Dutch survive here as immigrant-community languages in Argentina, Brazil and Suriname.

name: Top Spoken Languages: North America
tagline: Name North America's most-spoken languages from memory
description: North America's top languages by native speakers. Type as many as you can before time runs out.
metaTitle: Top Spoken Languages in North America Quiz
metaDescription: Can you name North America's most-spoken languages by native speakers? Free typing quiz — race the clock before time runs out.
guide: English and Spanish dominate this list, together accounting for the overwhelming majority of the continent's population, from Canada down through Mexico and Central America.

Haitian Creole and French are a distant third and fourth, carried by Haiti and Quebec respectively, ahead of Nahuatl and K'iche' — the two largest Indigenous languages, spoken across central Mexico and the Guatemalan highlands.

This list stops at six rather than ten. Beyond K'iche', a long tail of Mayan and other Indigenous languages are all genuinely spoken by real communities, but sources disagree enough on their relative size that ranking them further would be guesswork dressed up as data.

name: Top Spoken Languages: Oceania
tagline: Name Oceania's most-spoken languages from memory
description: Oceania's top languages by native speakers. Type as many as you can before time runs out.
metaTitle: Top Spoken Languages in Oceania Quiz
metaDescription: Can you name Oceania's most-spoken languages by native speakers? Free typing quiz — race the clock before time runs out.
guide: English leads, carried by Australia and New Zealand, ahead of Tok Pisin, Fijian, Samoan, Tongan and Maori.

Papua New Guinea alone is home to roughly 840 languages — more than any other country on Earth — but almost all of them have only a few thousand speakers, so none individually cracks a continent-wide top list the way a single Nigerian or Indian language can.

This list stops at six rather than ten for the same reason North America's does: past this point the ranking stops reflecting anything real and starts reflecting which obscure language a particular source happened to measure.

name: Landmarks by Country
tagline: Pick the landmark that belongs to a country
description: The landmark quiz reversed: you get a country and choose which of four famous sites is actually there.
metaTitle: Landmarks by Country — Which Landmark Is in Each Country?
metaDescription: Play a free landmarks quiz in reverse. Given a country, pick which famous landmark is found there, with a fact for every answer.
guide: Going this direction is harder than it sounds. Most people hold landmarks as pictures with a loose sense of somewhere abroad attached; asked to start from the country instead, that loose association stops being enough.
The wrong answers are always real landmarks in other countries, so every question quietly teaches you four placements rather than one. Over a round that adds up faster than the forward version.
The sixty landmarks here sit in forty-five countries across all six inhabited continents, so a full round covers a lot of ground.

name: Landmark Quiz
tagline: Find the country behind famous landmarks
description: From the Taj Mahal to Table Mountain — name the country each landmark stands in, and pick up a fact about it on the way.
metaTitle: Landmark Quiz — Which Country Is This Landmark In?
metaDescription: Play a free landmarks quiz. Identify the country behind 60 world-famous landmarks and learn a fact about each one.
guide: Landmarks are a sideways route into geography. You almost certainly recognise Petra, Machu Picchu and the Sydney Opera House already; what this game tests is whether you know which country each one stands in.
That gap is common and worth closing. Plenty of people can picture Angkor Wat without being able to name Cambodia, or the Great Mosque of Djenné without placing Mali.
Every answer comes with a fact about the landmark, so a round doubles as a short tour. The 60 sites here span all six inhabited continents.
